title: Hunt: The Shell Door
story: A teammate shipped this code. Read it like an attacker and tap every risky line.

tests.label: Find every risky line, then pick the fix

hints: Look for places where outside input reaches something powerful.
socratic: Compare your result with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what attack does this code allow?
code:
import os

def ping(host):
    cmd = "ping -c 1 " + host
    os.system(cmd)
    return True

why_lines.4: The host text becomes part of a shell command. A value like 1.1.1.1; rm -rf ~ adds a second command.
why_lines.5: os.system hands the whole string to a shell, which obeys every ; and && in it.

fix.question: Which is safer?
options: subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", "1", host]) after checking host looks like a hostname
fix.why: A list of arguments with no shell means ; has no special meaning, and validating the host adds a second layer.
